result.summary: SkyScene: fixed inset-0 z-0 pointer-events-none wrapper with a CSS sky-top/mid/bottom gradient underneath (no-flash + no-WebGL fallback, both wrapped in error boundaries) and an R3F Canvas (dpr [1,1.5], antialias/alpha/high-performance, fov 40 at z=10). frameloop is 'always', switches to 'never' on document.hidden and to 'demand' under prefers-reduced-motion (static frame, re-rendered on scroll via invalidate; no drift/float/mouse parallax). Sky.tsx: clip-space fullscreen triangle with a dithered sRGB-mixed gradient (#0c2d6e/#0d59c2/#2ea3ff) driven by scrollState.progress: deeper/cooler to 0.85 (top #08215a), then night (#061a3d/#0b2c5c) for the footer. Clouds.tsx: three procedural cumulus layers (gaussian lobes squashed for flat bases + domain-warped fbm silhouette detail + a 4-step light march that shades bellies Twilight-Blue and keeps tops white; tinted/dimmed at night) rendered at half resolution into two render targets — far+mid composited behind the glass wordmark, near composited in front — with per-layer horizontal drift (0.005/0.008/0.012 u/s), scroll parallax (near moves most), lerped mouse parallax, ~45% hero coverage getting slightly sparser down the page, near layer dropped on <768px with devicePixelRatio>1.5. GlassWordmark.tsx: Pacifico TTF fetched and parsed at runtime (src/sections/sky/ttf.ts, Suspense fallback null so sky+clouds render immediately) into drei Text3D (size 1, height 0.28, bevel 0.05, 12 curve segments), measured via bounding box and scaled to 87% (92% mobile) of the viewport width, MeshTransmissionMaterial (transmission 1, thickness 0.25 local ≈1.5 world, roughness .06, ior 1.45, CA .04, anisotropicBlur .1, distortion .15/.3/.1, resolution 768 or 512 at dpr>1.25, 6 samples) lit by a procedural Lightformer-only Environment (soft top rect, back-left ring rim, sky-blue fill). 6s ±0.12 float, mouse rotation ±0.06/±0.03 lerped at 0.05, scroll lift of 1.4× its height eased out over 0.9·innerHeight with an opacity fade on the last half, then mesh+material hidden (also skips the transmission FBO passes). All listeners, render targets, materials, geometries disposed on unmount; pnpm typecheck is clean. Shaders and the RT/composite pipeline were verified live in a standalone three r186 harness (compile, look, scroll/night states); the font parser was verified in node against Pacifico (9 shapes, sane bbox).
deviations: Font loading: three r186's examples/jsm/loaders/TTFLoader.js imports opentype.js from a jsdelivr URL at module-evaluation time (opentype.js is not installed and packages may not be added), which would make the whole page depend on a third-party CDN at runtime. Replaced with a small in-repo TrueType glyf parser (src/sections/sky/ttf.ts) producing the same typeface FontData shape for drei Text3D, plus a Suspense-style resource instead of useLoader.

Clouds are not three perspective planes: each layer is a fullscreen triangle rendered at half resolution into one of two render targets (behind / in front of the wordmark) and composited with premultiplied blending. Same depth layering and parallax behaviour, about 4x cheaper for the noise-heavy shader.

Cloud density uses summed gaussian lobes + mass noise + fbm detail with a short light march for shading rather than pure fbm thresholds; pure fbm produced smoke-like wisps rather than distinct cumulus in live tests.

MeshTransmissionMaterial thickness is set in local units (0.25 x text size) because the material multiplies thickness by the model scale; the fitted group is scaled ~2-3x, giving ~1.2-2 world units as intended.
Cloud coverage thresholds are absolute density values fitted numerically to the hero viewport (~18/20/14% per layer) instead of the nominal ranges in the brief.
risks: The React/drei integration (Text3D + MeshTransmissionMaterial + Lightformer Environment, half-res cloud pass ordering via useFrame priority -2) is typechecked but was not run in the app (no dev server allowed); the GLSL and RT/composite pipeline were verified only in a standalone three.js harness.
Procedural coverage varies by sky region: the hero composition is deterministic (fitted at the start offsets) but density after long drift or deep scroll can be noticeably sparser/denser.

Performance: the transmission material re-renders the scene into a 768^2 (512^2 on high dpr) FBO every frame while the wordmark is visible and the extruded text is ~200k vertices; low-end GPUs may dip below 60fps in the hero. Cloud pass is already half-res; lower Text3D curveSegments/bevelSegments or MTM samples if needed.

ACES tone mapping applies only to the glass (sky/cloud materials are toneMapped=false), so the refracted sky inside the letters reads slightly deeper than the surrounding sky; set toneMapped={false} on the material for a clearer look if preferred.

Back-cloud composite sits at clip depth 0.995 and depth-tests against the wordmark (~0.99 at 10 units with near 0.1/far 60); changing the camera near/far/position requires adjusting that constant in Clouds.tsx.
Fonts: only the glyphs of hero.wordmark are parsed; changing the wordmark to characters outside the TrueType cmap would render '?' glyphs (CFF/OTF fonts are not supported by the parser).

result.summary: Built the fixed 72px transparent Header per the brief. Root is fixed/top-0/z-100 with pointer-events none (nav, actions, visible wordmark and open mobile panel re-enable them), `transition: all .85s var(--ease)`, plus a masked rgba(0,0,0,.1)→transparent legibility overlay. Inner uses `.grid-air.grid-air--hero` as a flex row. Left nav renders `nav.items` (16px/500, gap 32 → 16 at ≤1024); items with columns get a button trigger (aria-expanded/aria-haspopup/aria-controls) with a 16px ChevronDown rotating 180° when open, and a `data-theme="light"` mega menu panel (white, radius 12, blur 12, padding 20; closed opacity 0/scale .96/translate -10px + visibility/inert, open in 350ms var(--ease)). Columns are 403px lists (300 at ≤1024) with optional 14px/60% titles, 56px haze icon squares with 20px icons mapped from item.icon, 16px titles, 13px @50% descriptions, ArrowUpRight 14px on external items, hover haze bg (.5s), and per-item stagger via `--i * 80ms` transition-delay; items with `cta` get the 403px haze CTA card (padding 24, radius 8, gap 24, secondary Button). Open on mouseenter, close on mouseleave with a 120ms grace timer (plus an invisible 16px hover bridge above the panel), pointer click toggles, keyboard focus-visible and Enter open, blur out of the item closes, Escape closes and refocuses the trigger, click outside closes; only one panel open at a time. Center `<a href="#">` with `<Wordmark size={26}/>` absolutely centered, opacity 0→1 (.5s) once `scrollState.y > 0.8 × innerHeight` via `useScrollListener` with a stable callback and a boolean state that only flips at the threshold; tabIndex/aria-hidden/pointer-events follow visibility, no layout shift. Right: tertiary Members, primary Join, secondary Partner (gap 8) and a 38×38 bordered hamburger (Menu→Close). At ≤768 the nav, tertiary and secondary hide; the white light-themed mobile panel drops from the top (padding 24 0 0, bottom radii 12, blur, 350ms, max-height 100dvh scrollable with data-lenis-prevent) with a black Wordmark + close button row, accordion rows (border-bottom rgba(0,0,0,.2), padding 24 0, chevron, sub-list max-height 0→2000px in .3s listing sub-items with the 56px haze icon squares) and a footer row with primary + secondary buttons at calc(50% - 4px). Lenis stop()/start() locks scroll while open; any link click, Escape, or crossing to ≥769px closes it and focus returns to the burger. Reduced motion disables all header transitions and the stagger delay. All timers/listeners/matchMedia subscriptions are cleaned up on unmount; icons are aria-hidden; `pnpm typecheck` passes.
deviations: Mega menu panels are anchored to the nav's left edge (nav is position:relative, items static) rather than to each item, at every breakpoint. Anchoring per-item let the 3-column Community panel (3 × 403px + padding) overflow the viewport between ~1025 and ~1420px; anchoring to the nav keeps the panel's `max-width: calc(100vw - 48px)` guarantee valid everywhere. Columns are `flex: 0 1 403px; min-width: 0` so they shrink proportionally at narrow tablet widths instead of overflowing.
Item stagger index (`--i`) restarts per column so parallel columns animate together (rather than a single global index across all 10 Community items, which would put the last item ~800ms behind).

Keyboard trigger activation (click with event.detail === 0 / Enter) always opens rather than toggling, so Tab-focus opening followed by Enter does not immediately close the panel; pointer clicks toggle as specified.

Hamburger and mobile close buttons use aria-label strings 'Open menu' / 'Close menu' that are not in content.ts (content.ts has no such labels; these are non-visible accessibility attributes, not copy).
risks: The wordmark visibility threshold reads window.innerHeight on each scroll event; it is not re-evaluated on a pure resize without scroll, so a rare resize-without-scroll could leave the state one step stale until the next scroll event.

The `inert` attribute is used on closed panels (supported in React 19 types and all evergreen browsers); very old browsers ignore it, but the visibility:hidden fallback still removes closed panels from the tab order.

The mobile panel lives inside the fixed header root; the header's `transition: all .85s` on the root does not affect the panel, but if another section later adds `overflow: hidden` to the header root the panel would be clipped.
Mobile panel content is limited to the viewport via max-height:100dvh with internal scrolling (data-lenis-prevent); on browsers without dvh support it falls back to unbounded height.

result.summary: Built the AgenticCards section (id="agentic"): SectionText (u-h2-large title, subtitle, primary white "Join QairuHub" button) from content.agentic; a 48px typewriter pill absolutely centered in a 48px row (white/10 fill, 28x21 sparkle area with Sparkle scaled 1.5, 16px text) whose text WIDTH animates 0 -> measured width over 800ms ease-out using an aria-hidden absolutely-positioned twin span for measurement, with a 2x24 currentColor caret that blinks via scale-y while typing and hides after; cycle = type 800ms -> hold 2200ms -> collapse 400ms -> next prompt, starting only when the pill scrolls into view. Three cards in a Grid (Col large=4 / medium=6 / small=12, 24px gutters) as <article tabIndex=0> with aspect-square monochrome CSS mock media (Learn: fanned 3-card session stack with date chip + skeleton lines; Build: 2x2 bento with Team/Repo/Demo/Sprint tiles and tiny glyphs; Launch: floating panel with 4 label+toggle/checkbox rows plus a tall product silhouette) and p-5 body (h3.u-h2 title, p.u-body-1 at fg/60). Active card = prompt index % 3 (switches when a new prompt starts typing); inactive cards opacity .4, active opacity 1 + border white/30, transitions 600ms var(--ease); hover (mouse pointer only) or keyboard focus makes a card active and pauses the cycle at the hold step, leaving resumes. Active cards get subtle synced micro-motion in the mocks (fan spreads, toggles flip on, checks fill, bars grow). Pill row and each card wrapped in <Reveal index={i}>. Reduced motion: full prompt shown, crossfade every 3.4s, all card/mock transitions instant, no caret. All listeners/timeouts/observers cleaned up; text width truncates with ellipsis on narrow viewports instead of overflowing; typecheck passes.
deviations: The bento tile labels 'Team', 'Repo', 'Demo', 'Sprint' are hardcoded in the component (as the brief instructed) rather than coming from content.ts; they are decorative (inside an aria-hidden media area).
The pill row is placed inside <Grid><Col large=12> so its 100% width (used to cap the text width on mobile) equals the content width rather than the full section width.
The typing cycle starts only once the pill row is ~30% in view (IntersectionObserver) so the first prompt's typing animation is actually seen, instead of starting on mount.
Cards carry a subtle rgba(fg,.06) fill + backdrop-blur(4px) (per the spec's flat-card language) in addition to the 1px white/10 border named in the brief.
risks: The available text width for the mobile ellipsis is computed with a PILL_CHROME constant (86px = padding 20+20, icon 28, gap 8, caret 2+8); if the pill padding/icon sizes are changed in CSS the constant must be updated in the TSX too.
Hover pause uses pointer events filtered to pointerType 'mouse', so touch taps do not pin a card; keyboard focus does pin/pause (by design).
At 1024px (medium=6) the third card sits alone on a second row, left-aligned, as the brief's column spec implies.
Not visually verified in a browser (dev server / build runs were disallowed); only tsc --noEmit was run.

result.summary:
Built the Logos section:
with a centered u-h4 title from logos.title via SectionText, then a (1600px, side padding removed via .logos__grid so the marquee runs edge to edge under AutoCarousel's built-in mask) holding two -wrapped rows (gap 80, itemHeight 80, 8px --v-gap between rows). Row 1 = logos.items at 45s; row 2 = items rotated by half at 55s, direction reverse. Each item is a text wordmark placeholder (white at 90% opacity, vertically centered, nowrap, data-logo-placeholder="true") styled per hint: caps = Inter 700 18px uppercase .08em; sans = Inter 600 22px; mono = ui-monospace 18px; serif = Georgia/Times 22px; script = var(--font-cursive) 30px 600. result.summary: Built the Waitlist (Accelerator) section, id="accelerator". Top block: Grid/Col (8/10/12 cols) + RevealGroup .text-air with Pill "Spring 2027", u-h2 two-line title (second line in <i> cursive), u-body-1 body (max-w 48ch), and a centered wrapping form row: ghost .input-air (371px, 100% on <=768) + primary submit Button. Submit preventDefaults, runs a basic email regex (aria-invalid + focus on failure) and swaps the row for a 16px confirmation line that fades in (local state, aria-live). Media card (Reveal delay 200, 10/12 cols): radius 20, overflow hidden, 16/9 (min-height 260 on mobile), flat #cfd4db surface, faint 12-column overlay (eleven interior 1px lines at white/12), centered u-h2-large caption (max 22ch, balanced), and a bottom step row (padding 32 / 20 mobile) of 32px pills (white/35 fill, white 14px text; 12px on mobile) joined by 2px tracks. The row is driven purely by CSS: a registered @property --wl-p animates 0 -> 1 linearly over N*1.5s (6s for 4 steps) and resets; each track's fill scales with its slice and the current pill flips to white fill / dark text (short 150ms cross-fade at each boundary) in exact sync. Animation pauses offscreen via useInView (once:false) + .u-animation-paused. Reduced motion (CSS media query): no animation, line fully drawn, last step highlighted, confirmation fade disabled. pnpm typecheck passes clean.
deviations: content.ts has no confirmation copy under `waitlist`, so the post-submit line reuses `form.successTitle` ("You are on the list.") rather than hardcoding text.

Step-row sync is implemented with one animated registered custom property (@property --wl-p) instead of a setInterval/animation-delay scheme; this keeps the line fill and the highlighted pill in exact sync with zero JS timers and no per-frame state.

Reduced motion is honoured via the CSS `prefers-reduced-motion` media query rather than window.matchMedia in JS, since the section has no JS-driven motion (reveals are handled globally in global.css).
risks: @property (registered custom property animation) is required for the smooth line fill and pill switching: Chrome 85+, Safari 16.4+, Firefox 128+. Older browsers degrade to a discrete jump at the cycle midpoint (same baseline as the existing AnimatedBorder in global.css). color-mix() is used for the pill text colour with a plain `color: var(--white)` fallback declared first.
White u-h2-large caption on the light #cfd4db surface has low contrast (~1.5:1), as specified by the brief for this video stand-in; flag if WCAG text contrast is required there.
At 375px the four-pill step row fits with ~20px to spare; if `waitlist.demoSteps` labels get longer or more steps are added, the row could clip inside the card on narrow screens.

result.summary: Built the Supersize section (id="supersize", default padding, gap none). An <h2 class="u-h1"> renders supersize.text from content.ts split into inline-block word spans (real space text nodes between them keep natural wrapping). The heading is left-aligned with 24px left padding (16px at <=768), no right padding, white-space normal / no forced breaks, and its box is calc(100% + 18vw) wide so the last word of a line bleeds off the right edge while the section clips with overflow-x: clip (page never scrolls sideways). Verified against real Anton hmtx metrics via a scratch TTF parser: 1440 -> 3 lines "BUILDERS OVER / TALKERS. SHIP / EVERY SEMESTER." (~900px section), 1024 and 768 -> 3 lines, 375 -> 5 lines with every word fully visible. Scroll-linked reveal: a rAF loop (started on mount, cancelled on unmount) early-outs when scrollState.y is unchanged and nothing invalidated it, otherwise maps elementProgress(section) from 0.25..0.75 to 0..1 and, only when p changed, writes per word t = clamp(p*N - i + 0.5), opacity = 0.15 + 0.85t, translate3d(0,(1-t)*12px,0) directly on refs (no setState). Resize and document.fonts.ready invalidate the cached progress. Reduced motion: matchMedia check (plus change listener) stops the loop and sets all words to opacity 1 / no transform; a CSS @media fallback does the same statically. Listeners and rAF are cleaned up on unmount. pnpm typecheck passes with zero errors.
deviations: The section element is located via textRef.current.closest('.supersize') instead of a ref on <Section>, because the shared Section component does not accept/forward a ref (typecheck rejected it) and components/ui is off-limits.

Word spacing uses real whitespace text nodes between the inline-block spans (React Fragments with ' ') rather than a trailing space inside each span or margin-right .22em: a trailing space inside an inline-block is collapsed away, and margin-right would count toward line width at wrap points; text nodes give exact natural wrapping and clean screen-reader output.

The heading box is calc(100% + 18vw) wide (one em wider than the viewport). With a 100%-wide box the sentence wraps to 4 lines at 1440 (~1120px section) because 'EVERY SEMESTER.' measures ~1650px; the widened box produces the 3-line wrap and ~950px height the brief calls for, with the last word bleeding the right edge as in the reference.
No cursive <i> word was added: supersize.text in content.ts does not mark one and the brief specifies an all-uppercase Anton poster line.
risks: The 3-line wrap at 1440 means 'SEMESTER.' is clipped by roughly its last two glyphs (bleed ~235px); this is the intended poster effect but if the client wants the whole word visible, drop the width to calc(100% + 10vw) (4 lines, ~1120px tall) or accept a 4-line layout.

The rAF early-out keys on scrollState.y (fed by Lenis). If scrolling ever happens without Lenis emitting (e.g. Lenis destroyed), the words would only update on resize/font-ready; under the current SmoothScroll wrapper this does not occur.
Verified with tsc only (no dev server/screenshots allowed); wrapping was validated numerically from the Anton font's advance widths, which should match browser layout closely but not to the pixel.

result.summary: Built the ProductDemo section (id="demo"). Stage: <Grid center><Col large={10} medium={12}> with a relative 1400/860 stage (1/1.15 on mobile) holding three absolutely-positioned, role="tabpanel" items that cross-fade via opacity .8s var(--ease) (inactive: opacity 0 + pointer-events none + aria-hidden). Each holds a light data-theme="light" app-window mock (80% width, radius 10, white bg, 12px text): 40px top bar with signal-blue dot avatar + app name, centered 24px haze search pill, Upload ghost pill + Create 24px black filled pill; 180px #fafafa sidebar listing app.sidebar with 14px icons (Grid2, Calendar, Users, Folder, CheckCircle, Book) and a haze-highlighted active item per screen; main area renders schedule (date 11px @50%, title 12px, 20px haze chip), leaderboard (rank, team, project, 4px progress track with black fill at 88/72/58/44%, chip) or cohort (4 haze kanban columns, radius 8, padding 8, counts[i] white mini cards with two skeleton lines). Tab bar: <Grid center><Col large={8} medium={12}> .pd-tabbar (36px, white/10 + blur(4px), radius 10, padding 2, role="tablist") with three real <button type="button" role="tab" aria-selected aria-controls> tabs (flex 1, u-body-3, gap 6, 14px Sparkle/Bolt/Rocket icons, opacity .5 / active opacity 1 + var(--black)), roving tabindex + Arrow/Home/End keyboard nav, and a sliding indicator (rgba(255,255,255,.95), radius 8, left var(--x)/width var(--width), .5s var(--ease)) measured from the active button's offsetLeft/offsetWidth on mount, change, ResizeObserver and document.fonts.ready. Inside it a 3px rgba(0,0,0,.14) timer bar animates width 0→100% linearly over productDemo.autoAdvanceMs (restarted via key), then auto-advances; clicking a tab selects it and restarts the timer; the timer (JS timeout + CSS animation-play-state) pauses while offscreen (useInView once:false) or while the document is hidden, resuming with the leftover time. Reveal: stage via <Reveal>, tab bar via <Reveal delay={150}>. Reduced motion: no auto-advance, no timer bar, instant swaps/indicator. Responsive to 375px: sidebar collapses to 44px icon rail, Upload hidden, leaderboard project column hidden, kanban 2 columns, stage overflow clipped. All listeners/observers/timeouts cleaned up. pnpm typecheck passes.
deviations: Mock-chrome labels 'Search or ask…', 'Upload' and 'Create' are not in content.ts; they are defined as a CHROME constant in ProductDemo.tsx exactly as named in the brief (all product copy still comes from productDemo).
Class is named .pd-tabbar (scoped) rather than a global .tabbar to avoid collisions with other sections' CSS.
The brief's '#fafafa' sidebar fill is used as given; the avatar dot uses the Signal Blue token (var(--signal-blue)) since no colour was specified.
Stage cross-fade uses the brief's .8s (the DESIGN-SPEC mentions 500ms); the brief was treated as authoritative.
risks: Could not run the dev server or take screenshots per the rules, so responsive breakpoints (1440/1024/768/375) were verified by reasoning about the CSS rather than visually.
On the 375px layout the schedule/leaderboard titles rely on text-overflow ellipsis inside the mock; very long content rows would truncate rather than wrap.
Section is wrapped in a single flex-column div (gap 48px) inside <Section> so the in-view observer can hold both the stage and the tab bar; this mirrors the section's own 48px gap.

result.summary: Built the Features section (id="features", spacing="large"): SectionText with u-h3 title (cursive "at scale") + body, then a content-width Grid of 7 AnimatedBorder cards laid out 7/5 · 5/7 · 4/4/4 (medium mirrors large, small = 12). Each Col is flex so cards stretch to equal row height; each card is wrapped in <Reveal index={i} stagger={200}>. Card box `.feature`: radius 12, overflow hidden, rgba(fg,.06) fill + backdrop blur 4px, hover .09 over .6s var(--ease); text block padding 32 (24 mobile) gap 8 with h3.u-h5 + p.u-body-1-alt. The first four cards carry a flex-1 media area (padding 0 32 32 / 0 24 24) with a monochrome mock panel (radius 11, .06 fill, 1px .12 border): schedule (4 rows: 12px time @50%, 13px truncating title, 24px chip — rows reuse productDemo.app.schedule.rows), chart (8 columns, 24px bars 35–100% tall at .85, 11px value labels above, 20px tiles below; bars scale down to 12–16px on ≤420px), links (36px search pill with Search icon + skeleton line, two stacked link cards with 40px thumbnail, two skeleton lines and a 14px ArrowUpRight), timeline (10 weekly dots, milestone dots at weeks 1/4/7/10 labelled from productDemo.app.cohort.columns, progress fill to week 7). One useInView observer on the grid wrapper (once:false, threshold 0) pauses the border strokes offscreen and, on first sight, adds `.is-in` which plays the mock entrance transitions (rows/links fade-up, bars scaleY, timeline fill scaleX, labels fade) using var(--ease). Reduced motion: matchMedia seeds the seen state to true and a CSS media block removes all transitions so mocks render static in their final state (AnimatedBorder/Reveal already handle their own fallback in global.css). All colours use rgba(var(--fg-rgb), .x)/var(--fg); radii limited to 4/8/11/12/9999; no shadows or gradients. `pnpm typecheck` passes with zero errors.
deviations: Timeline milestone labels come from content.ts (productDemo.app.cohort.columns = Idea / MVP / Traction / Demo Day) instead of the brief's hardcoded 'Kickoff, MVP, Traction, Demo Day', to honour the no-hardcoded-copy rule; only decorative numbers (chart values 42–100, 10 weeks, fill to week 7) are local constants.
Schedule mock rows reuse productDemo.app.schedule.rows (date / title / type) rather than invented text, for the same reason.

The Reveal wrapper sits inside each Col (as a full-width flex child) rather than being the Col itself, so the column width math from .col-air stays intact; visually identical (each card fades/slides with the 200ms stagger).
The section stub used id="Features"; changed to id="features" as the brief and nav anchors require.
risks: Not visually verified in a browser (no dev server allowed); layout math was reasoned from global.css. At 375px the schedule chip text ('Talk + build slot') is clamped to 96px with ellipsis and the title truncates, which is intended but worth a glance in screenshots.

Value labels above chart bars are positioned by the bar's percentage height; if a designer later changes the track height the labels follow automatically, but the 100% bar's label sits 6px above the track top and relies on the panel's 20px padding for room.

AnimatedBorder's paused state adds `u-animation-paused` which pauses CSS animations only; the mock entrance effects are transitions, so they are unaffected (by design) but will not replay if the grid leaves and re-enters the viewport.

result.summary: Built the ModelsCTA section (id="cta") per the brief: Section > Grid > Col(12) > Reveal > AnimatedBorder(radius 12) wrapping `.ctacard` (relative, overflow hidden, radius 12, padding 40 / 24 on <=768, rgba(var(--fg-rgb),.06) fill, flex space-between center gap 24, column + align-start on <=768). Left `.ctacard__content` (z2, max-width 500, column gap 8): h2.u-h3.cursive title, h3.u-h5 subtitle, p.u-body-1 body, all from `ctaCard` in content.ts. Right: secondary Button linking to ctaCard.cta.href (opens in new tab since it is an external GitHub URL). Orbs: `.ctacard__orbs` (absolute inset 0, z1, pointer-events none) > `.ctacard__orbs-inner` (140% square centred, rotates 26s linear infinite) with three `.orb` children (55% square, blur 70px, opacity .85, colours #4c96f7 / #d8d36a / #e5aad8 at left5%/top10%, right0/top20%, left35%/bottom0) each pulsing scale .55->1.45 alternate infinite at 9s/12s/15s (negative delays so they desync), plus an rgba(0,0,0,.12) overlay for text legibility. Reduced motion is honoured twice: a `window.matchMedia` hook adds `.ctacard--static` (orbs at scale 1, no rotation) and a CSS `prefers-reduced-motion` block does the same. Orb animations and the AnimatedBorder stroke are paused via `u-animation-paused` while the card is offscreen (useInView once:false) to keep the 70px blurs cheap. `pnpm typecheck` passes with zero errors.
deviations: The global `.cursive` class sets font-size 1.18em of the parent, which at the same specificity as `.u-h3` would shrink the fully-cursive title to ~19px; ModelsCTA.css therefore overrides `.ctacard__content .u-h3.cursive` to clamp(30px, 2.7vw, 38px) (30px on mobile) so it lands at the u-h3 x 1.18 scale the spec implies.
The three orbs are given negative animation-delays (-4s, -8s) so their pulses are desynchronised from the first frame; the brief specifies only the durations.
The CTA link (an external GitHub URL) is rendered with target=_blank; the Button component adds rel=noreferrer automatically. Anchors starting with # stay in-tab.
risks: Three 70px-blurred orbs plus a rotating 140% container are GPU-heavy; animations are paused offscreen and under reduced motion, but low-end devices may still see some jank while the card is in view.

The h2 uses `.u-h3 cursive` exactly as briefed, so the headline inherits Caveat 600 italic; if the global cursive rule ever changes line-height/size, the local override in ModelsCTA.css should be revisited.
Colours #4c96f7 / #d8d36a / #e5aad8 are raw hex values by design (named in the brief as the one colourful moment); they are the only non-token colours in the section.

result.summary:
Built the Integrations section:
with a centered u-h4 h2 title (titleBefore + cursive + titleAfter from content.ts) via SectionText, then a > > > single marquee row. Each item is an IntegrationTile (80x80, radius 12 via --radius-cards, bg rgba(var(--fg-rgb),.08), 1px border rgba(var(--fg-rgb),.12), flex-centered, padding 8, 12px/600 white text clamped to 2 lines) with style variants caps (uppercase, .06em tracking), mono (ui-monospace), serif (Georgia), script (var(--font-cursive) 18px italic); sans is the default. Tiles carry data-logo-placeholder="true" and accept an optional `src` prop that renders an instead of the text, with a comment describing how to swap in real logos. Reduced motion: a small useReducedMotion hook (window.matchMedia with change listener cleanup) passes `paused` to AutoCarousel, in addition to the global CSS that already stops the track animation and makes reveals instant. All copy comes from content.ts; no new hex colours; CSS lives in the co-located Integrations.css. `pnpm typecheck` passes with zero errors.
deviations: Tile text weight is 600 as the brief requires, which is above the spec's general 'no UI text > 500' rule; the tiles are logo placeholders rather than body text, so the brief was followed.
`line-clamp: 2` is emitted alongside the `-webkit-line-clamp` form; the unprefixed property is not yet universally supported and is harmless where ignored.
risks: The section is not visually verified in a browser (dev server/build was out of scope); layout relies on the shared .carousel/.grid-air/.col-air classes, which already handle overflow clipping and the edge mask.

The AutoCarousel mask (transparent->black 20%->80%->transparent) fades tiles near the edges; at 375px the visible area between fades is about 200px, so roughly one full tile is fully opaque at a time, which matches the reference behaviour but reads sparse on very narrow screens.
No integrations item in content.ts uses the 'script' style, so that variant (Caveat 18px) is styled but currently unexercised.

result.summary: Built the Storytelling triptych (Section id="story", spacing none). Root .triptych is a calc(100lvh*4.5) runway with margin-top -50vh; .triptych__inner is sticky top 0 / 100lvh / overflow hidden; .triptych__content is a 1fr/1fr grid with padding-top var(--header-height) and place-items center; the three story.items share grid cell 1/1 as centred flex columns (h2.u-h1-small uppercase title + p.u-body-1 body in a 560px max-width block, margin-top 8, 0 24 padding / 0 16 mobile). A single rAF loop reads scrollState.y + root getBoundingClientRect, computes P = clamp(-top / (height - innerHeight)), t = P*3 - i with the i=0 max(t,.3) and i=N-1 min(t,.7) clamps, enter = smoothstep(-.15,.3), exit = smoothstep(.7,1.15), opacity = enter*(1-exit), translateY = (1-enter)*120 - exit*120, scale = .96 + .04*enter*(1-exit), and writes opacity/transform/pointer-events (none below .05) straight to item refs with change-detection so untouched frames cost nothing; work is skipped when scroll/viewport are unchanged or the runway is far offscreen (after one forced initial pass). Reduced motion (window.matchMedia, followed live) switches to the .triptych--static layout — auto height, no margin/sticky, items in normal flow with 120px gaps — rendered via <Reveal index={i}>. rAF, resize listener, ResizeObserver and matchMedia listener are all cleaned up on unmount, and inline styles are reset when the loop stops. pnpm typecheck passes with zero errors; the curve values were verified numerically at P = 0, 1/3, 2/3, 1 and in between.
deviations: Items 1 and 2 carry an initial inline style { opacity: 0, pointerEvents: 'none' } so all three do not stack visibly during the single frame before the rAF loop's first write; the loop overwrites it immediately.

Added a ResizeObserver on document.body (in addition to the window resize listener) so layout shifts above the runway (font swap, lazily mounted sections) resync the items without waiting for a scroll event.
CSS declares a 100vh fallback ahead of each 100lvh value for browsers without dynamic viewport units.
The <Section> receives aria-label="How QairuHub works" so the sticky region is an identifiable landmark for assistive tech; not requested, purely additive.
risks: margin-top -50vh overlaps the tail of the Integrations section (as in the reference); because Storytelling is later in DOM order it paints above it, so any tall/low content at the bottom of Integrations will be covered by item 0 during that 50vh.

On mobile browsers the runway height uses 100lvh while progress uses window.innerHeight; while the browser toolbar is visible the sticky stage can be taller than the visible area by the toolbar height, so the centred item may sit slightly low until the UI collapses (inherent to the reference's lvh choice).
Only pnpm typecheck and a numeric evaluation of the curves were run — no dev server or screenshots (per the brief), so visual proportions at 1440/1024/768/375 were not eyeballed in a browser.

result.summary: Built the DemoForm section (id="join"): SectionText u-h2-large two-line title with cursive ship + body from content.form; centered 7/8/12-col Reveal'd white `.formcard` (data-theme="light", radius var(--radius-cards), padding 40 / 24 on mobile, overflow hidden). Controlled form (noValidate, flex column gap 16): first/last name row (flex 1 1 200px, wraps at 375), email, telegram, year + source selects (placeholder option value "" disabled hidden, data-empty for placeholder colour), message input, centered primary Submit disabled until valid, u-body-3 legal (max-width 400, opacity .5, Signal Blue underlined links). Required: first, last, email (regex), telegram, year, source; blur-marks fields with `.is-invalid` border rgba(var(--red-rgb),.6) and a 12px `--red` helper (local var --red: #ee3238 in DemoForm.css), with aria-invalid/aria-describedby/role=alert and sr-only labels. Submit → 600ms fake async (form aria-busy, button disabled) → `.formcard__success` overlay (absolute inset 0, white, radius 12, flex column center gap 8, u-h4 successTitle, successBody, tertiary "Send another" resets values/touched/status); the form is `inert` while the overlay shows, focus moves to the overlay then back to the first input after reset. Focus ring inside the card: 2px rgba(0,0,0,.5). Overlay entry uses an 800ms var(--ease) fade/rise, disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. Timer cleared on unmount; pnpm typecheck passes with zero errors.
deviations: content.ts has no validation or reset copy, so four semantic UI strings live in a local MSG const in DemoForm.tsx: 'This field is required', 'Please choose an option', 'Enter a valid email address', and the 'Send another' label named in the brief.

Card and overlay background use var(--white) (token, resolves to #fff) instead of a literal #fff, per the no-new-hex rule; the error red rgba(238,50,56,.6) is expressed as rgba(var(--red-rgb), .6) with --red-rgb defined next to --red locally.
The SectionText title is wrapped in a <span id> so the section can carry aria-labelledby; visual output is identical (the .u-h2-large i cursive rule still matches the nested <i>).
Success overlay entry is animated (800ms fade + 12px rise, var(--ease)) rather than appearing instantly; reduced-motion shows it static.
risks: Not visually verified in a browser (dev server/build were off-limits); layout was reasoned from global.css: at 375px the card inner width is ~295px so the name row stacks, at 768px+ it stays two-up.

The `inert` attribute on <form> relies on React 19 typings (typecheck passes) and modern browser support; older browsers simply ignore it, leaving the covered form focusable via keyboard behind the overlay.

Disabled primary button inherits the global .btn:disabled style (haze fill, grayscale, 50% opacity) which inside the light card reads as a light grey ghost — matches the brief's 'haze disabled style' but could be tuned if the reference looks different.
The message field is a single-line <input> (brief: 'message input', .input-air is 48px); if a multi-line textarea is wanted it needs a height override.

result.summary: Footer section: <footer id="footer" data-theme="dark"> 150vh, flex/align-end, overflow hidden, root pointer-events none with content re-enabled. Content pinned at bottom (var(--row-margin)) inside <Grid hero> + <RevealGroup>: left nav of footer.links (16px/500, external ones with 14px ArrowUpRight, target _blank rel noreferrer, hover opacity .6 / .3s) and right column of five icon <Button variant="icon"> socials (1px rgba(fg,.3) border, radius 9999, 18px icons) plus u-body-3 copyright at .6; stacks/centres at ≤768. GrassScene: R3F <Canvas> mounted lazily (useInView rootMargin 150%, once), dpr [1,1.5], alpha true (transparent so the fixed night sky shows through), flat tone mapping, frameloop driven by state: 'never' when document.hidden or footer >1 viewport away, 'demand' + a few invalidates for reduced motion (static frame), else 'always'. Scene: 700-star ShaderMaterial points with twinkle (no fog), PlaneGeometry 80x40/160x80 hills displaced by the brief's h(x,z) with vertex colours darkening toward the valley/bottom (MeshStandardMaterial #2f8f3a), InstancedMesh grass (20 000 desktop / 6 000 mobile or dpr>1.5) of tapered 0.07x0.9 blades on the hill surface with random yaw/height 0.6–1.3, per-instance colour, custom vertex shader bending along uv.y² with wind sin(uTime*1.4+x*.35+z*.6)*.35 + gust term, fog chunks, DoubleSide; 7 red five-petal flowers on stalks and 2 red-cap mushrooms with white dots that sway; glass 3D wordmark (hero.wordmark) via drei <Text3D> from a typeface generated at runtime by three's TTFLoader (Pacifico TTF) sized to ~55% (80% mobile) of the viewport width at y 3.2, bobbing ±0.1 / yaw ±0.05, <MeshTransmissionMaterial transmission 1, thickness 1.2, roughness .08, ior 1.45, chromaticAberration .04, distortion .15, temporalDistortion .1, resolution 512> refracting the navy night (background colour) + grass; procedural <Environment> from three <Lightformer>s, hemisphere light #6a8bd6/#1b4a22, directional moon from upper-left, fog #07142e 12→40. Camera fov 45 at (0,1.6,9) looking at (0,1.8,0) is treated as the design frame for the bottom 100vh of the 150vh canvas, with setViewOffset extending the projection upward (extra sky above while scrolling in). Geometries/materials/observers/listeners/timeouts disposed on unmount; no per-frame allocations or setState. No-WebGL fallback: SVG hill silhouette (#2a7f33) across the bottom 45%. pnpm typecheck passes.
deviations: TTFLoader is consumed through a thin Loader subclass (LazyTTFLoader) that dynamically imports three/examples/jsm/loaders/TTFLoader.js inside load(), still via useLoader. Reason: that three module statically imports opentype.js from a jsDelivr CDN URL; a static import would make an offline/blocked-CDN visitor lose the entire page (module graph up to App.tsx), whereas now only the wordmark fails and SceneErrorBoundary swallows it.

Camera: because the canvas is 150vh (not one viewport), the brief's fov-45 camera is applied as the design frame for the bottom 100vh and the projection is extended upward with camera.setViewOffset (camera.manual = true so r3f leaves it alone). Without this the wordmark at y=3.2 would sit above the fold at the page bottom and the composition would be vertically stretched over 1.5 viewports.
Blades right in front of the lens (z > 6.5) are eased down by up to 30% so they don't fill the whole bottom of the frame; everywhere else heights are the specified 0.6–1.3.

The render loop also runs while the footer is within one viewport (rootMargin 100%) rather than only when on screen, so shaders and the 20k-instance upload are compiled/warm before the footer becomes visible.
Scene-only colours not named in the spec were chosen for the flower pistil (#f4c542), mushroom stem cream (#f3e9d2) and the moon light tint (#cdd8ff); all UI colours use tokens.
risks: The glass wordmark depends on opentype.js loading from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net at runtime (three's TTFLoader hard-codes this). Offline or with the CDN blocked the wordmark is simply absent (grass/stars still render). If a network-free build is required, a pre-generated typeface JSON in public/ would be the fix.

Visual tuning (light intensities, grass brightness, transmission look, fog) was done by reasoning only; the brief forbids running the dev server, so the first live look may need small adjustments to lighting/shade constants in GrassScene.tsx and shaders.ts.

MeshTransmissionMaterial renders the scene into a 512px buffer every frame (a second pass over the 20k-instance grass); on low-end GPUs with dpr 1.5 this could dip below 60fps. Reducing `samples` or `resolution`, or BLADES_DESKTOP, are the knobs.
Per the brief, any device with devicePixelRatio > 1.5 (most retina laptops) gets the 6 000-blade mobile count, which reads sparser than the 20 000 desktop field.
The SkyScene builder is expected to darken the fixed sky to night over the last 15% of the page; the footer canvas is transparent and relies on that (fog colour #07142e is matched to a navy night).

fixed: src/sections/footer/GrassScene.tsx: replaced the CDN-dependent LazyTTFLoader (three's examples/jsm TTFLoader imports opentype.js from jsdelivr at runtime) with the in-repo useTTFFont parser from src/sections/sky/ttf.ts, so the footer glass wordmark no longer depends on a third-party CDN and shares the hero's cached Pacifico parse; removed the now-unused useLoader/FontData imports and the emitted TTFLoader chunk. Typecheck and build clean; footer wordmark verified rendering after the change.
remaining: Single JS chunk of 1,265 kB (354 kB gzip) contains three + drei + fiber + app; under the 1.5 MB gzip threshold, no code-splitting done.

Hero performance risk (per SkyScene builder): MeshTransmissionMaterial re-renders into a 768^2/512^2 FBO every frame while the wordmark is visible and the extruded text is ~200k vertices; low-end GPUs may dip below 60fps in the hero. Untested on real hardware (screenshots were software-rendered by Playwright).
Storytelling sticky section duplicates the LAUNCH frame in desktop shots at y9900 and y10800 (expected: last slice holds LAUNCH), which is by design per spec; no gap seen.

Header mega menu, mobile panel, typewriter pill, tab bar auto-advance and form submission were not exercised interactively in this round (only static scroll screenshots); no console errors during load/scroll at any breakpoint.

findings.summary: The footer wordmark renders as an opaque dark-navy slab, not glass: MeshTransmissionMaterial is given `background={new Color(SCENE.fogColor)}` (#07142e) so the transmission pass refracts a near-black backdrop, and thickness 1.2 attenuates whatever light is left (verified in desktop-14/15, tablet-15, mobile-16: letters are solid #0b1a3a with no see-through, no sky/cloud refraction).
findings.fix: Replace the solid fog colour with a night-sky gradient backdrop so the glass has something to refract: build a small CanvasTexture (e.g. 4×256, vertical gradient #061a3d → #12386f matching Sky.tsx NIGHT palette, colorSpace SRGB) in the useMemo at line 369 and pass it as `background`; drop `thickness` from 1.2 to ~0.4, set `color="#dfe9ff"`, `roughness={0.1}`, keep ior 1.45; raise the two Lightformer intensities in Lighting() (2.2→4, 1.4→2.5) so rims read as glass highlights like the hero wordmark.

findings.summary: At 375px the centred header wordmark collides with the right-hand actions: `.hdr__logo` stays `left:50%; translate:-50% -50%` on mobile, so the ~130px Pacifico wordmark (≈122–252px) is overlapped by the 'Join QairuHub' button (≈186–310px) once the logo fades in (verified in mobile-01, mobile-03, mobile-09, mobile-16).
findings.fix: Inside the existing `@media (max-width: 768px)` block (line 393) add: `.hdr__logo { position: static; translate: none; margin-right: auto; }` and `.hdr__inner { justify-content: flex-start; }` so the wordmark sits at the left edge in flow (the nav is hidden there) and the actions keep `margin-left:auto`; alternatively pass `size={22}` and cap `.hdr__logo { max-width: calc(100vw - 220px) }`.

findings.summary: On desktop the hero glass wordmark reads as a smeared blue blur with barely legible glyphs (desktop-00 zoom: 'Qairu' is a streaked slab, the 'H' has no readable shape) while the same scene at 768/375 is crisp — the transmission FBO is fixed at 768px (512 at dpr>1.25) although the letter run is ~1250px wide at 1440, so the refraction is upscaled ~1.9× and then blurred further by `anisotropicBlur={0.1}`.
findings.fix: Size the FBO to the drawn width: `const resolution = Math.min(1024, Math.round(size.width * Math.min(viewport.dpr, 1.5)))` (keep the 512 cap only when `isMobile && viewport.dpr > 1.5`), and on the material (line 114) set `anisotropicBlur={0.02}`, `distortion={0.08}`, `roughness={0.03}` so glyph edges stay sharp and the clouds refract as distinct shapes instead of a smear.

findings.summary: The product-demo app window fills only 80% of the 10-col stage (`.pd-app { width: 80% }` inside a 1400/860 stage): at 1440 the white window is 732×457px instead of spanning the ~914px column the spec assigns ("app window card, 10 cols"), leaving ~90px of empty sky on each side of the stage and a small, low-impact mock (verified desktop-05).
findings.fix: Set `.pd-app { width: 100%; }` and change `.pd-stage { aspect-ratio: 16 / 10; }` (line 11) so the window is the stage; drop the `@media (max-width:1024px) .pd-app { width: 88% }` override (line 372) since the width is now 100% everywhere.

findings.summary: Cloud silhouettes read as defocused blobs rather than cauliflower cumulus: every layer is rendered into a half-resolution target (`RT_SCALE = 0.5`) and the `softness: 0.13` edge ramp plus bilinear upscale erase the fbm4 detail, so edges look Gaussian-blurred in every desktop frame (most visible desktop-00/03/09).
findings.fix: Render the near layer sharper: use `RT_SCALE = 0.75` (or 1.0 for the `front` target only) and lower `softness` to 0.08 on the front layer (line 34) / 0.10 on the mid layer (line 33); keep the far layer at 0.13 so depth still reads.

findings.summary: At 768px the waitlist email input is forced to 100% width (736px) and the 'Notify me' button wraps to a second centred row, breaking the spec's single input+button row much earlier than necessary (verified tablet-04).
findings.fix: Change the breakpoint on the `.input-air.wl-input { width: 100% }` rule from `(max-width: 768px)` to `(max-width: 480px)` so the 371px input + button stay on one row at tablet widths and only stack on phones.

findings.summary: In the integrations title the cursive `whole` visually touches `ecosystem` — the Caveat italic glyphs overhang their advance and the trailing space in `titleAfter` collapses to about half a normal word gap (verified desktop-08 zoom).
findings.fix: Append `#integrations .u-h4 i { margin-right: 0.18em; }` to Integrations.css so the cursive word gets the same optical gap as the space before it.

findings.summary: Every in-page anchor (header nav, mega-menu items, 'Join QairuHub', CTA, footer links, and the header wordmark href="#") performs a native instant jump instead of a Lenis smooth scroll — Lenis is created without the `anchors` option and nothing calls lenis.scrollTo, so the page's scroll-linked motion (supersize wipe, triptych, sky) is skipped on every click.
findings.fix: Pass `anchors: { offset: -72 }` (Lenis 1.3 supports it) in the `new Lenis({...})` options; in Header.tsx give the `.hdr__logo` and `.hdr__m-logo` links an onClick that calls `e.preventDefault(); lenis?.scrollTo(0)` because an empty hash (`#`) is not handled by Lenis' anchor handler. Note `smoothWheel: !reduce` is redundant — Lenis 1.3 already honours prefers-reduced-motion via `respectReducedMotion: true`.

findings.summary: Mobile accordion sub-menus animate `max-height: 0 → 2000px` in 0.3s, so opening completes in ~30ms (measured 0px → 392px within one frame) and closing sits still for ~100ms before collapsing — no visible open motion, delayed close.
findings.fix: Replace the max-height hack: `.hdr__m-sub { display:grid; grid-template-rows:0fr; transition: grid-template-rows .35s var(--ease) } .hdr__m-sub.is-open { grid-template-rows:1fr } .hdr__m-sub-inner { min-height:0; overflow:hidden }` (keep `inert` toggling).

findings.summary: The mobile panel only fades in with a 10px nudge (`translate: 0 -10px → 0`), whereas the spec describes a white panel dropping from the top over 350ms.
findings.fix: Use `translate: 0 -100%` (or `clip-path: inset(0 0 100% 0)`) in the closed state of `.hdr__mobile` and `translate: 0 0` / `inset(0)` in `.is-open`, keeping `transition: all .35s var(--ease)`; keep opacity 0→1 if desired.

findings.summary: Mega-menu item stagger index restarts at 0 for every column (`col.items.map((item, i)` → `index={i}`), so in two-column menus (Community) both columns animate in parallel instead of each item following the previous one by 80ms.
findings.fix: In `Columns`, keep a running offset across columns (e.g. `let n = 0` before the map and pass `index={n++}` to each `SubItem`) so `--i` increases through the whole panel.

findings.summary: App-window screens cross-fade over 0.8s (`transition: opacity 0.8s`, measured ~800ms), but the spec (§4.7) specifies a 500ms cross-fade.
findings.fix: Change `.pd-stage__item { transition: opacity 0.5s var(--ease) }`.

findings.summary: The typewriter caret is only shown during the 800ms typing phase (`typing = phase === 'typing'`) and disappears for the whole 2.2s hold, so with a 760ms blink period it blinks at most once and the prompt sits caret-less while fully typed.
findings.fix: Keep the caret blinking while the prompt is on screen: `const typing = !reduced && (phase === 'typing' || phase === 'holding')` (hide it only for 'collapsing'/'idle').

findings.summary: The hero glass wordmark only bobs vertically and turns with the mouse; it has no slow idle rotation (spec §4.2 'slow float/rotation'), unlike the footer wordmark which does (`sin(t*0.4)*0.05`).
findings.fix: Add an idle yaw/pitch to the targets: `const targetY = (reduced ? 0 : pointer.x * ROT_Y) + (reduced ? 0 : Math.sin(t * 0.4) * 0.04)` and similarly `targetX += Math.sin(t * 0.5 + 1) * 0.015`, keeping the existing ROT_LERP smoothing.

findings.summary: Progress math uses `window.innerHeight` while the CSS runway/stage use `100lvh`; on mobile browsers with a collapsible URL bar the range (`rect.height - innerH`) and the centred stage no longer match the visible viewport, shifting the enter/exit timing and the vertical centre of each item.
findings.fix: Measure the sticky stage instead: keep a ref to `.triptych__inner` and use `const innerH = inner.getBoundingClientRect().height` for `range` (and for the near-viewport skip test), so JS and CSS agree on the lvh-based height.

findings.summary: Storytelling and Supersize (src/sections/Supersize.tsx:79) each run their own never-ending requestAnimationFrame loop for the whole session (alongside Lenis' loop and two r3f canvases) even when the section is far offscreen, while the shared `addTick` loop in src/lib/ticker.ts sits unused.
findings.fix: Replace the local `raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick)` loops with `const off = addTick(tick)` from lib/ticker.ts (return `off` from the effect), and gate the tick with an IntersectionObserver (rootMargin ≈ '100% 0px') so it only runs when the section is near the viewport; delete the dead `useTick`/`useScrollY` helpers or start using them.

findings.summary: The initial scroll seed only sets `y` and `limit`; `progress` stays 0 until the first Lenis scroll event, so on a reload mid-page the sky/cloud uniforms (which read `scrollState.progress`) render the day palette for one or more frames before snapping.
findings.fix: Seed all fields: `const limit = Math.max(1, document.documentElement.scrollHeight - window.innerHeight); setScroll({ y: window.scrollY, limit, progress: window.scrollY / limit })`.

findings.summary: Nav anchors `#events`, `#about`, `#members`, `#programs`, `#community`, `#resources` and `#privacy` (lines 53, 74, 104, 107, 119, 121, 361, 369-371) point at ids that do not exist on the page, so clicking Events/About/Members and the footer links does nothing (only #agentic, #logos, #accelerator, #supersize, #demo, #features, #cta, #integrations, #story, #join, #footer resolve).
findings.fix: Point them at existing section ids (e.g. Events → '#demo' or '#features', About → '#story', Members → '#join', Programs → '#features', Community → '#agentic', Resources → '#integrations', Privacy → a real URL) or add matching ids to the sections.

findings.summary: At 375px the centered header wordmark (.hdr__logo, 133–242px) sits under the right-hand "Join QairuHub" primary button (183–313px): once the logo fades in after the hero (every mobile shot from y812 on) the button covers ~60px of the wordmark, so the mobile header is not "primary button + hamburger" and the logo reads as "Qairu" cut off. The collision exists for every viewport narrower than ~508px.
findings.fix: In the `@media (max-width: 768px)` block add `.hdr__logo { left: 16px; translate: 0 -50%; }` (left-align the wordmark in the 16px page margin, like the mobile panel's .hdr__m-logo; the 108px mark then ends at 124px, well clear of the actions at 183px). Alternatively hide it: `.hdr__logo { display: none; }` on ≤768.

findings.summary: At 1024px the centered wordmark (450–559px) overlaps the last nav link "About" (440–485px) — verified live: the header renders "AbQairuHub" once the logo becomes visible (scrollY > 80vh). The absolutely-centered logo ignores the nav width, so any width under ~1180px collides.
findings.fix: In `@media (max-width: 1024px)` (or a new `@media (max-width: 1180px)`) hide the centered mark: `.hdr__logo { display: none; }` — or shrink the nav so the center stays free: `.hdr__list { gap: 12px; } .hdr__link, .hdr__trigger { font-size: 14px; }` and keep the logo only at ≥1181px.

findings.summary: Between 769px and ~868px (verified at 820px, iPad Air portrait) the desktop header does not fit: nav list needs 461px but its flex box shrinks to 397px (min-width:0) and the overflowing "About" link (440–485px) runs under the actions group that starts at 437px; total content (24 + 461 + 16 + 344 + 24 = 869px) exceeds the viewport.
findings.fix: Make the 769–1024 band fit: in `@media (max-width: 1024px)` add `.hdr__secondary { display: none; }` (nav 461 + gap 16 + Members/Join 201 + margins 48 = 726px ≤ 769px), or move the mobile header breakpoint up (`@media (max-width: 1024px) { .hdr__nav, .hdr__login, .hdr__secondary { display:none } .hdr__iconbtn, .hdr__mobile { display:... } }`) and mirror the matchMedia in Header.tsx line 199 (`(min-width: 1025px)`).

findings.summary: When the mobile panel is open at 375px, the header's white "Join QairuHub" primary button and its black label are painted on top of the white panel (visible at the top of the panel between the wordmark and the close button in the live screenshot) because `.btn span` (z-index 2) and `.btn--primary::after` (z-index 1) sit in the header's stacking context while `.hdr__mobile` has z-index auto; the header's burger (now an X) also stacks on top of the panel's own close button (17–55px vs 24–62px).
findings.fix: Give the panel its own layer above the bar: `.hdr__mobile { z-index: 5; }` and hide the bar's controls while it is open: `.hdr.is-mobile-open .hdr__actions { visibility: hidden; }` (the panel already has its own close button and CTA buttons).

findings.summary: At 768px (≤768 is the `small` breakpoint, so the three cards stack to 12 cols) `.ac-card__media { aspect-ratio: 1/1 }` produces a 719px-tall media square per card: each card is 847px tall and the three cards alone span ~2.6k px of the tablet page (tablet-02/03 shots show one card filling a whole 1024px viewport, mostly empty translucent mock).
findings.fix: Cap the square when the card is full-width: in a `@media (max-width: 768px) and (min-width: 481px)` block add `.ac-card__media { aspect-ratio: 16 / 10; }` (or `aspect-ratio: auto; height: 420px;`), keeping 1/1 only below 480px where the media is ~343px. Alternatively use `small={6}` for the first two cards in AgenticCards.tsx line 339 (`<Col large={4} medium={6} small={6}>` for i < 2) so 768 gets the 2+1 layout.

findings.summary: At 768px the app-window card is 721×829px (`.pd-stage { aspect-ratio: 1/1.15 }` + `.pd-app { height: 100% }`): the mock content (4 schedule rows) ends at y≈292px inside the card, leaving ~600px of blank white (tablet-06 shot is a white sheet), whereas the same rule is fine at 375px (343×394).
findings.fix: Scope the tall ratio to phones and use a landscape ratio for tablets: `@media (max-width: 768px) { .pd-stage { aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; } .pd-app { width: 100%; height: 100%; aspect-ratio: auto; } }` plus `@media (max-width: 480px) { .pd-stage { aspect-ratio: 1 / 1.15; } }` — or drop the fixed ratio and let the card size itself: `.pd-stage { aspect-ratio: auto; }` with `.pd-stage__item { position: relative; }` for the active one and `.pd-app__main { min-height: 220px }`.

findings.summary: The `width: calc(100% + 18vw)` bleed lets the final word run 237px past the viewport at 1440px ("semester." spans 651–1677px, clipped by the section's overflow-x: clip) and past the edge at 768px with fallback metrics (tablet-05 shot shows "EVERY SEMEST"), so the sentence reads "SHIP EVERY SEMESTE" — the poster bleed cuts a whole syllable plus the period instead of a few pixels.
findings.fix: Reduce the allowed bleed to a fraction of one glyph and prefer wrapping: `width: calc(100% + 0.35em);` (≈90px at 1440) so "semester." wraps to its own 4th line at 1440 and fits at 1024/768/375; keep `overflow-x: clip` on `.supersize`. If a bleed is required, add `padding-right: 0.15em` and `text-wrap: pretty`.

findings.summary: Footer text links are 24px tall (16px/1.5 line-height, no padding) at 375px (measured 24px hit areas, 32px apart on mobile), below the ≥38px touch-target size used everywhere else (icon buttons are 38×38).
findings.fix: Enlarge the hit area without changing the visual rhythm: `.footer__link { padding: 7px 0; margin: -7px 0; }` (24 + 14 = 38px) and on ≤768 bump the row gap `.footer__nav { gap: 12px 20px; }` so adjacent rows' hit areas do not overlap.

findings.summary: Body copy sits directly on the live sky where bright white clouds drift behind it (visible in shots/r1/desktop-07-y6300.png: 'Qairu Space' / 'Open Playbooks' text is unreadable) and the fixed gradient bottom (#2ea3ff) gives full white only 2.69:1 and 60% white 1.83:1; 60% white on sky-mid #0d59c2 is 3.36:1, all below WCAG 4.5:1.
findings.fix: Give every text-bearing card a flat darkening fill instead of rgba(var(--fg-rgb), .06): use background: rgba(var(--black-rgb), .28) with the existing backdrop-filter in .feature, .ac-card (AgenticCards.css:130), .pd-tabbar and .ctacard__overlay; raise secondary text from .6/.5 to .8 (.ac-card__text AgenticCards.css:158, .footer__copy, .pd-tab inactive opacity ProductDemo.css:316, .formcard__success__body); for free-standing SectionText/nav add a text-shadow-free fallback by strengthening .hdr__shade to rgba(0,0,0,.35) and, per section, a `.section-air::before` fixed-position translucent black scrim at .18 (flat colour, not a gradient) so the 4.5:1 minimum holds even when a cloud passes behind the text.

findings.summary: The selected tab's focus ring is invisible: .pd-tab:focus-visible only sets outline-offset:-2px, so the inherited white outline rgba(var(--fg-rgb),.8) is drawn inset on the white .pd-indicator behind the aria-selected tab.
findings.fix: Add `.pd-tab[aria-selected="true"]:focus-visible { outline-color: rgba(var(--black-rgb), .8); }` (or outline: 2px solid var(--black)) so keyboard focus is visible on the active tab; keep the white ring for inactive tabs.

findings.summary: Header/footer anchors point at ids that do not exist anywhere in the DOM (#programs, #community, #events, #resources, #about, #members, #privacy, #cookies, #instagram, #x, #linkedin), so the primary nav links, 'Members', footer links and three social buttons are dead clicks.
findings.fix: Map every href to an existing section id (#features for Programs, #story for Community/About, #demo for Events, #cta for Resources, #join for Members) or add the missing ids on the target sections (e.g. Features: id="features" plus a wrapper id="programs"), and replace placeholder social hrefs with real URLs or drop those socials until they exist.

findings.summary: Hash links are left to the browser: Lenis 1.3.26 is created without the `anchors` option, so in-page links jump instantly (no smooth scroll) and land under the fixed 72px header because nothing sets scroll-padding-top / a scroll offset.
findings.fix: Pass `anchors: { offset: -72, duration: 1.2 }` (Lenis ScrollToOptions) in the Lenis constructor (and `anchors: true` is enough when reduced motion is on), plus add `html { scroll-padding-top: var(--header-height); }` in global.css as the native fallback; alternatively intercept `a[href^="#"]` clicks and call `lenis.scrollTo(hash, { offset: -72 })`.

findings.summary: 12px legal text at opacity .5 on the white form card (black .5 on white = 3.32:1, and the Signal Blue links inherit the .5 opacity → even lower) and the 13px mega-menu descriptions at rgba(--fg,.5) (Header.css:189, :232) fail the 4.5:1 minimum for small text.
findings.fix:
Raise .formcard__legal to opacity: .7 (≈5.1:1) and move the opacity off the children (set color: rgba(var(--fg-rgb), .7) on the

instead of opacity on the container); change .hdr__sub-desc and .hdr__cta-desc to rgba(var(--fg-rgb), .65).

findings.summary: The production build emits a single 1,265 kB raw (354 kB gzip) JS chunk containing three + drei + fiber + the whole app, above the 1.2 MB threshold, and the footer GrassScene (only mounted 150% viewports before the end) is still in the initial chunk.
findings.fix: Add `build.rollupOptions.output.manualChunks: { three: ['three'], r3f: ['@react-three/fiber', '@react-three/drei'] }` so the vendor code caches separately, and in src/sections/Footer.tsx replace the static import with `const GrassScene = lazy(() => import('./footer/GrassScene'))` wrapped in `<Suspense fallback={null}>`; optionally also `lazy()` SkyScene in App.tsx since the CSS FALLBACK_GRADIENT already covers the first paint.

findings.summary: Mega-menu triggers use aria-haspopup="true" (announces a 'menu' and implies role=menu/arrow-key semantics) while the panel is a plain <div> with aria-label but no role, so screen readers announce a menu that never appears and the aria-label is dropped on a generic element.
findings.fix: Follow the APG disclosure-navigation pattern: remove aria-haspopup, keep aria-expanded + aria-controls, and give the panel `role="group"` (or `role="region"`) so its aria-label is exposed.

findings.summary: Each <article> card has tabIndex={0} but no interactive semantics or action, adding three empty tab stops whose only effect is a visual highlight; together with .ac-card opacity .4 (AgenticCards.css:135) inactive card text renders at ~24% white (1.65:1).
findings.fix: Drop tabIndex from the article (keep the hover highlight and the timer), or if keyboard highlighting is wanted make the card body a real control (e.g. a <button> that pins the prompt) and lift inactive opacity to .6 so the 16px body stays ≥3:1 on the darkest sky.

findings.summary: The submit button is `disabled` until the form is valid, so neither clicking nor pressing Enter can trigger onSubmit and the `setTouched(ALL_TOUCHED)` error-reveal branch is unreachable — users get no feedback about which required fields are missing until they blur every one.
findings.fix: Use `aria-disabled={!valid}` with a visual disabled style instead of the disabled attribute, keep the early-return in onSubmit that sets all fields touched, and focus the first invalid field after that call.

findings.summary: On an invalid email the input only gets aria-invalid and focus; no error text or aria-describedby explains what is wrong, so screen-reader users hear 'invalid' with no reason.
findings.fix:
Render a `

Enter a valid email address

` when `invalid` and add `aria-describedby={invalid ? 'wl-email-error' : undefined}` to the input.

findings.summary: <Footer> renders inside <main>, so the <footer> element is not exposed as the contentinfo landmark (footer/header only map to landmarks when not descendants of main/section/article).
findings.fix:
Move `

findings.summary: `gl.getClearColor(new THREE.Color())` allocates a new THREE.Color on every frame inside the priority −2 useFrame, creating GC churn in the hottest loop on the page.
findings.fix: Hoist a module-level `const PREV_COLOR = new THREE.Color()` and call `gl.getClearColor(PREV_COLOR)`; likewise reuse it in setClearColor.

findings.summary: journey.ts, quality.ts (detectQuality/getDpr tiers) and lib/ticker.ts are never imported anywhere — the documented quality tiers, DPR caps and shared rAF ticker are dead code while SkyScene/GrassScene hardcode dpr [1,1.5], 768/512 transmission resolution and 20000 blades.
findings.fix: Either delete the three modules or wire them: `const tier = detectQuality()` in SkyScene/GrassScene → `dpr={[1, getDpr(tier)]}`, `resolution={QUALITY[tier].transmissionRes}`, `samples={QUALITY[tier].transmissionSamples}`, `blades={QUALITY[tier].blades}` so low-end devices get the cheaper hero glass automatically.

findings.summary: .reveal keeps `will-change: opacity, translate` forever on every revealed element (dozens of cards, rows and headings), pinning compositor layers and memory long after the one-shot transition ended.
findings.fix: Remove `will-change` from .reveal (the 1s transition promotes on demand), or clear it once revealed: `.reveal.is-visible { will-change: auto; }` after a `transitionend` handler in Reveal.tsx.

findings.summary: SkyScene relies solely on a silent React error boundary for the no-WebGL case (no supportsWebGL() precheck like GrassScene, no componentDidCatch logging), so a missing context surfaces as a thrown render error in StrictMode/dev and gives no diagnostic in production.
findings.fix: Reuse the footer's supportsWebGL() check (`const [webgl] = useState(supportsWebGL)` and render the Canvas only when true) and add `componentDidCatch(e){ if (import.meta.env.DEV) console.warn('[sky] scene failed', e) }` to Boundary.

findings.summary: The documented 'swap in real logos' path is not wired: LogoMark accepts `src` but Logos never passes `item.src`, and `logos.items` in content.ts (line 176) is cast to a type without `src`, so following the comment at lines 27-34 yields a TS error and then a silent no-op; Integrations.tsx:65 has the identical gap.
findings.fix: In content.ts add `export interface LogoItem { name: string; style: 'caps'|'sans'|'mono'|'serif'|'script'; src?: string }` and type both `logos.items` and `integrations.items` as `LogoItem[]` (drop the `as` casts at lines 176 and 316); then pass `src={item.src}` in Logos.tsx:87 and Integrations.tsx:65.

findings.summary: There is no submission seam: the form fakes success with `window.setTimeout(…, FAKE_SUBMIT_MS)` and Waitlist.tsx:33 simply calls `setDone(true)`, so wiring a real endpoint requires editing component internals rather than swapping one function.
findings.fix: Create `src/lib/submit.ts` exporting `submitJoin(values: JoinValues): Promise<void>` and `subscribeWaitlist(email: string): Promise<void>` (initial bodies keep the 600ms fake); call them from DemoForm.onSubmit (await, then setStatus('success'), catch → error state) and Waitlist.onSubmit, and export the `Values` type so the user only touches submit.ts to integrate a backend.

findings.summary: Eleven hrefs in content.ts point at ids that do not exist on the page (#programs, #community, #events, #resources, #about, #members, #privacy, #cookies, #instagram, #x, #linkedin — page ids are agentic/logos/accelerator/supersize/demo/features/cta/integrations/story/join/footer/Hero), so the top-level 'Events'/'About' nav links, 'Members', most footer links and three socials are dead.
findings.fix: Point each to an existing section id (e.g. Programs→#features, Community→#story, Events→#demo, Resources→#cta, About→#agentic, Members/Instagram/X/LinkedIn→real URLs in brand.links, Privacy/Cookies→a real page) or add the missing anchors; add a comment listing the valid section ids next to `nav`.

findings.summary: Three modules are dead (zero importers): sky/journey.ts, sky/quality.ts and lib/ticker.ts; worse, their comments lie — ticker.ts:3 claims Supersize/Storytelling/Header use it (each runs its own rAF loop) and quality.ts:3 says 'never hardcode counts elsewhere' while GrassScene.tsx:14-16 hardcodes STAR_COUNT/BLADES_*.
findings.fix: Delete src/sections/sky/journey.ts, src/sections/sky/quality.ts and src/lib/ticker.ts (or, if the shared ticker is wanted, migrate Supersize.tsx:34-85 and Storytelling.tsx:48-118 onto `useTick` and remove their private rAF loops).

findings.summary: JOURNEY-SPEC.md states it 'supersedes §1 of DESIGN-SPEC' and describes a single-canvas space→sky→night backdrop with the footer as a DOM spacer, none of which is implemented (two canvases, no space phase, journey.ts unused) — the next builder will be misled.

findings.summary: `motion` is a declared dependency with zero imports anywhere in src, and README.md:15 claims 'motion where imperative', so both the lockfile and the docs advertise a library that is not used.
findings.fix: Run `pnpm remove motion` and change README.md line 15 to 'CSS transitions/keyframes + rAF loops (lib/scroll.ts)'; if imperative motion is planned later, re-add it when first used.

findings.summary: `useReducedMotion` is re-implemented five times (AgenticCards.tsx:26, ProductDemo.tsx:39, ModelsCTA.tsx:12 with a different initial value, Integrations.tsx:41, footer/useMediaQuery.ts:18) plus four inline matchMedia setups (Storytelling.tsx:20/37, Supersize.tsx:32, Features.tsx:128, SkyScene.tsx:36-41), with inconsistent SSR guards — AgenticCards.tsx:27 and SkyScene.tsx:36-38 read `window`/`document` in useState initialisers unguarded, which throws during an Astro/Next server render.

findings.summary: Two separate glass-wordmark implementations exist — footer GlassWordmark (GrassScene.tsx:362-429) and sky/GlassWordmark.tsx:92-123 — both building Text3D + MeshTransmissionMaterial + Environment/Lightformers + useTTFFont with divergent bevel/material numbers, so changing the sculpture's look means editing two places.

findings.summary: The TTF parser/loader is shared infrastructure but lives inside a section folder (sections/sky/ttf.ts) and is reached cross-section via `'../sky/ttf'`; it also deep-imports the `FontData` type from '@react-three/drei/core/useFont' (ttf.ts:10), a path that is not part of drei's public surface.

findings.summary: The sky palette hexes are copied from global.css tokens into three code files (Sky.tsx:11-13 DAY/NIGHT, Clouds.tsx:41-44 TWILIGHT/NIGHT_*, GlassWordmark.tsx:13 `SKY_BOTTOM = '#2ea3ff'`), so editing `--color-sky-*` / `--color-twilight-blue` changes the CSS fallback gradient but not the WebGL sky, clouds or glass fill light.
findings.fix: Add src/sections/sky/palette.ts exporting `SKY = { top: 0x0c2d6e, mid: 0x0d59c2, bottom: 0x2ea3ff, twilight: 0x426188, nightTop: 0x061a3d, nightBottom: 0x0b2c5c }` with a comment that it mirrors global.css @theme, and import it in Sky.tsx, Clouds.tsx and GlassWordmark.tsx (or read the vars once via getComputedStyle in SkyScene and pass them down).

findings.summary: Two parallel token namespaces describe the same values — Tailwind `@theme` (`--color-haze`, `--color-ink`, `--ease-air`, lines 42-66) and the `:root` block (`--haze`, `--black`, `--ease`, lines 69-97) — and every section uses the `:root` names, so a user retheming via the Tailwind tokens sees utilities change while all components keep the old colours.
findings.fix: Alias the `:root` vars to the theme tokens: `--white: var(--color-whiteout); --haze: var(--color-haze); --black: var(--color-ink); --black-void: var(--color-black-void); --signal-blue: var(--color-signal-blue); --twilight-blue: var(--color-twilight-blue); --ease: var(--ease-air);` and keep the `-rgb` triplets next to them with a comment that they must be kept in sync.

findings.summary: Sections read other sections' copy: Features.tsx:19 renders `productDemo.app.schedule.rows` and Features.tsx:76 `productDemo.app.cohort.columns` inside feature-card mocks, and Waitlist.tsx:52 shows `form.successTitle` as the waitlist confirmation — editing the product-demo or form copy silently changes unrelated sections.

findings.summary: Section CSS introduces raw hexes the spec does not name: DemoForm.css:5 `--red #ee3238` (the only semantic status colour, with no token), ModelsCTA.css:82/88/95 orb colours, ProductDemo.css:133 `#fafafa`, Waitlist.css:53 `#cfd4db` (its comment at line 4 claims the brief names it; DESIGN-SPEC §4.5 only says 'light haze/grey glass surface'), and ProductDemo.css:86/144 `rgba(27,27,27,…)` instead of `rgba(var(--black-rgb),…)`.

findings.summary: The logo placeholder tile is implemented twice — LogoMark (Logos.tsx:36, Logos.css:48-82) and IntegrationTile (Integrations.tsx:24, Integrations.css:44-63) — each with its own caps/sans/mono/serif/script font switch and its own `src` branch, so the user replacing placeholders with real assets must change two components and two stylesheets.

findings.summary: `id="Hero"` is the only capitalised section id (all others are lowercase) and is referenced by nothing, while the header wordmark links use a hardcoded `href="#"` (Header.tsx:312 and 356) instead of a content/brand value.

findings.summary: `DUR` presents itself as the source of truth for durations but only `DUR.typewriter` is read; reveal/stagger/dropdown/tab/header values are duplicated as literals in global.css:284-286, Header.css:109 and ProductDemo.css:345, and `EASE`, `EASE_CSS`, `lerp` (ease.ts:2,3,19), `useScrollY` (SmoothScroll.tsx:66) and `setScroll`'s export have no consumers.

findings.summary: Small helpers are copy-pasted: `smoothstep`/`smooth` in Storytelling.tsx:15, Sky.tsx:23 and Clouds.tsx:50; `EMAIL_RE` in Waitlist.tsx:13 and DemoForm.tsx:29; the fullscreen-triangle geometry in Sky.tsx:30-34 and Clouds.tsx:52-57.

findings.summary: Two near-identical error boundaries exist (SkyScene.tsx `Boundary` at line 12 and footer/SceneErrorBoundary.tsx), differing only in the DEV console.warn.
findings.fix: Move footer/SceneErrorBoundary.tsx to src/components/three/SceneErrorBoundary.tsx, give it the optional `fallback` prop it already has, and use it in SkyScene.tsx in place of the local class.

findings.summary: `const material = useRef<THREE.ShaderMaterial>(null)` is attached at line 117 but never read — a dead ref left over from an earlier uniform-update approach.
findings.fix: Delete the `material` ref and the `ref={material}` prop on the stars `<shaderMaterial>` (uniforms are already driven through the memoised `uniforms` object).

findings.summary: `window.__lenis = instance` (with a `declare global` augmentation at lines 7-11) is set unconditionally, leaking a debug handle onto the global in production builds.
findings.fix: Wrap with `if (import.meta.env.DEV) window.__lenis = instance` (and the matching `delete` at line 49), or remove it and rely on `useLenis()`.

findings.summary: `[key: string]: unknown` index signatures on RevealProps (line 62) and RevealGroupProps (line 108) accept any prop name, so typos like `classname` or invalid DOM attributes pass typecheck.
findings.fix: Replace the index signature with `extends Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, 'style' | 'className'>` and keep `as?: ElementType`; do the same for RevealGroupProps.

findings.summary: The section element is located with `textRef.current?.closest('.supersize')`, a class-name DOM query that silently breaks if the class is renamed, instead of a ref on the Section.
findings.fix: Add `const sectionRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null)` and pass `ref={sectionRef}` to `<Section>` (Section spreads `...rest` onto the tag, and React 19 passes `ref` as a prop), then use `sectionRef.current` in the effect.

findings.summary: `footer.links` mixes objects with and without `external`, so the inferred type is a union and Footer.tsx:42 has to write `'external' in link && link.external === true`; likewise `hero.wordmark` (line 129) duplicates `brand.name` (line 11) although the header/footer `Wordmark` renders `brand.name` and the 3D scenes render `hero.wordmark`.
findings.fix: Declare `export interface FooterLink { label: string; href: string; external?: boolean }` and type `footer.links: FooterLink[]` (Footer.tsx then uses `link.external === true`); set `hero.wordmark: brand.name` so there is one wordmark string.

findings.summary: GPU resources (render targets, materials, geometries) are allocated inside `useMemo` (Clouds.tsx:88-152, Sky.tsx:30-55, GrassScene.tsx:131/170/182/276) and disposed in effects; React StrictMode double-invokes memo initialisers in dev, so one orphaned set of GL objects is created per mount during development.

[motion] In-page anchors now scroll with Lenis instead of jumping natively. Implemented via the finding's allowed alternative (intercept `a[href^="#"]` clicks and call `lenis.scrollTo`) rather than Lenis' `anchors` option, after verifying in lenis 1.3.26 source that `anchors` (a) never calls preventDefault, so the browser's synchronous fragment jump lands first and the glide then starts from the pre-click position — a one-frame flash — and (b) ignores an empty `#` hash. A bubble-phase document click listener resolves same-page hash links (skips modified/non-left clicks, target=_blank, download, other pages, defaultPrevented, and unknown ids so missing anchors like #about fall back to native), prevents default, and defers one frame to `scrollToAnchor(lenis, hash, { push: true })` — deferral matters because Header calls lenis.stop() while the mobile menu is open and `start()` → `reset()` kills any in-flight animation. Scroll-linked scenes (supersize wipe, triptych, sky) now run on every click.

Also exported `scrollToAnchor()` and `ANCHOR_OFFSET` for any component that wants to trigger the same behaviour imperatively.

[motion] Removed redundant `smoothWheel: !reduce`; set `respectReducedMotion: true` explicitly (Lenis forces lerp → 1 and makes programmatic scrolls immediate under prefers-reduced-motion, matching spec section 6 'Lenis smoothing off').

Deep links on load are also corrected — one frame after mount, if location.hash resolves to an element and the browser's fragment jump is evident (target flush with viewport top), it is nudged by the offset with `immediate: true`; reload scroll-restoration is left untouched.

[a11y-perf] URL hash is kept in sync via history.pushState (top links strip the hash), so deep-linking and back/forward keep working despite preventDefault. Keyboard/AT focus moves to the target on complete like native fragment navigation (transient tabindex=-1 with the focus ring suppressed only for that transient focus, cleaned up on blur).
